rationale: C15 provides a highly concrete template for the child: both are further-retirement-exemption orders whose recital identifies the official, describes an earlier exemption and its duration, invokes the public interest, and leads to an operative clause using the same statutory authority and the formula “I hereby further exempt the said [official] from compulsory retirement.” C14 shares the specialized further-exemption recital structure, while C23 closely matches the authority clause and fixed one-year exemption machinery but concerns an initial rather than further exemption.

shared_material.child_excerpt: who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of three years by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... be further exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below
shared_material.parent_excerpt: who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of seven months ... by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... be further exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel recital identifying the prior exemption, its term, and the need for a further exemption.

shared_material.child_excerpt: by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 404 (5 U.S.C. 715a)
shared_material.parent_excerpt: by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30 1932 47 Stat. 404 (5 U.S.C. 715a)
shared_material.explanation: The same specific statutory authority is invoked with nearly identical wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby further exempt the said Lawrence M. Lawson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1953
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby further exempt the said Harry B. Mitchell from compulsory retirement for are for an indefinite period of time
shared_material.explanation: The operative command follows the same specialized formula, with the official and duration changed.
